name: An upper limit on electron antineutrino mass from Troitsk experiment

significance.quote: This gives an experimental upper sensitivity limit of mν < 2.2 eV , 95% C . L. and upper limit estimates mν < 2.12 eV , 95% C .L. for Bayesian statistics and mν < 2.05 eV , 95% C .L. for the Feldman and Cousins approach.

summary.plain: Re-analysing all its tritium data, the Troitsk experiment found no sign of a neutrino mass and limited it to about 2.1 to 2.2 electron-volts at 95% confidence, matching the Mainz result.
summary.technical: Re-analysis of the 1994-2004 data with careful data selection: m² = -0.67 ± 2.53 eV²; sensitivity limit mν < 2.2 eV, Bayesian limit 2.12 eV and Feldman-Cousins limit 2.05 eV (95% CL).

title: An upper limit on electron antineutrino mass from Troitsk experiment
why_it_matters: A direct limit of about 2 eV on the electron-antineutrino mass, of similar size to the final Mainz result of 2.3 eV that the paper cites.
